title: Vendor Technical Governance & Anti-Lock-In Playbook (Google + Systems Integrators)
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Google Workspace + Gemini enterprise transformation; architecture/governance/integration or migration work, live-environment care).

Google Admin console + Microsoft/Entra authored click-by-click from public docs; Gemini Enterprise preview/rolling-out capabilities cited or flagged 'verify in tenant', never invented; third-party migration-tool and enterprise-app internals deferred to vendor docs.
hook: Keep architectural control while partners do the work
problem: When Google and systems integrators drive execution, the enterprise can quietly lose architectural control and inherit long-term lock-in. This playbook makes you the primary technical counterpart: a repeatable way to validate vendor assumptions, review designs, challenge implementation approaches, and keep a clean separation between vendor execution responsibility and enterprise architectural authority — so partners deliver sustainable solutions without fragmentation or lock-in.
whats_inside: Governance Overview — the operating model between the enterprise architect and external partners (Google, integrators), and where authority sits.
Vendor-Design Review Method — how to review and validate vendor proposals against the target architecture, challenge assumptions, and require clean/sustainable patterns.
Anti-Lock-In Criteria — the checklist of portability, data-ownership, standards-conformance, and exit criteria every vendor design must meet; RACI separating execution vs architectural authority.
5 supporting scripts — vendor-deliverable inventory discovery, conformance/anti-lock-in validation, a review/finding report, remediation tracking, and a scope helper.
Escalation & a Vendor-Governance runbook — how to handle non-conformant designs, plus Testing gates and Best Practices for durable partner relationships.
short: A repeatable vendor technical governance method — validate assumptions, review designs, apply anti-lock-in criteria, and keep execution vs architectural authority cleanly separated — so partners deliver sustainable solutions. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
short_plain: A repeatable vendor technical governance method — validate assumptions, review designs, apply anti-lock-in criteria, and keep execution vs architectural authority cleanly separated — so partners deliver sustainable solutions.
meta_description: Govern Google + systems-integrator execution on a Workspace transformation: validate vendor assumptions, review designs, apply anti-lock-in criteria, and separate execution from architectural authority. Self-guided playbook and scripts.
bottom_line: Vendor execution that aligns to the target architecture — no long-term lock-in, no fragmentation — with architectural control firmly held by the enterprise.
